dedupe_keys.name: the national risk atlas of rwanda 2015

description: The National Risk Atlas of Rwanda is a 193-page national risk assessment published in 2015 by the Ministry of Disaster Management and Refugee Affairs and now hosted by MINEMA. It was co-financed by the ACP-EU Natural Disaster Risk Reduction Program managed by GFDRR, with support from UNDP. The foreword says it covers the five hazards that most affect Rwanda, namely droughts, floods, landslides, earthquakes and windstorms, as the first phase of national risk assessment, and that it is meant to guide planning in sectors such as transport, health, education, essential services, land use and building codes. Its chapters give base maps and data on population, land cover, education, health facilities, transportation, residential buildings and poverty; a method for hazard, exposure and vulnerability assessment with estimation of economic cost; and hazard mapping for each hazard with data sources, zonation maps, limitations and recommendations. Access is free as a PDF. The copyright notice allows reproduction for educational, research and non-profit purposes with acknowledgement, and forbids resale or commercial use without written permission. Caveats: the atlas dates from 2015, maps are in the PDF only, and other hazards were left for later phases. Coverage is Rwanda. It supports hazard exposure analysis of roads, health facilities and schools; related records are the NDMA Pakistan infrastructure risk atlas and ThinkHazard.
